Q01.text:
Annual leave > Eligibility

Permanent UK employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, plus England and Wales bank holidays. Part-time entitlement is pro-rated by contracted weekly hours. Contractors are outside this policy. The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December.

Sickness absence > Company sick pay

Permanent UK employees who have passed probation receive up to 10 working days of company sick pay at full base pay per calendar year. Employees still on probation should ask the People team about their pay arrangements. Statutory sick pay eligibility, rates and interaction with company pay are not specified here.

Enhanced parental leave > Scope and eligibility

This policy describes fictional enhanced company benefits for permanent UK employees with at least 26 weeks of continuous service by the expected week of birth or placement. Contractors are outside this policy. It does not provide a complete statement of statutory entitlements; ask the People team about statutory rights or eligibility outside this enhancement.

Annual leave > Carry-over

Up to 5 unused days may be carried into the next calendar year with line-manager approval recorded by 15 December. Carried days must be used by 31 March. This demo policy does not describe statutory exceptions or individual contractual arrangements; refer those questions to the People team.

Annual leave > How to request

Submit requests in PeopleHub at least 10 working days before the first day of leave. Your line manager approves or declines within 3 working days. Do not treat a submitted request as approved. Requests for more than 10 consecutive working days also need approval from Priya Shah, Head of People.

New starter onboarding > First month

Your line manager holds a check-in at the end of weeks 1, 2 and 4. Permanent UK employees may request hybrid working after their first 4 weeks, subject to role suitability and written line-manager approval under the remote working policy. The company home-office allowance is not an automatic joining bonus.

New starter onboarding > First week

Complete information security and code of conduct training within 5 working days of starting. Your line manager agrees your first-month goals by the end of working day 5. Read the annual leave, sickness absence and expenses policies before making related requests or claims.

Remote and hybrid working > Eligibility

Permanent UK employees whose roles can be performed remotely may request hybrid working after completing their first 4 weeks. Hybrid arrangements require written line-manager approval. Contractors must use their engagement agreement; this policy does not grant them hybrid eligibility.

Enhanced parental leave > Partner benefit

An eligible partner may take 4 weeks at full base pay. Take the leave in one block within 6 months of birth or placement. Only one employee may use the primary carer benefit for the same child; the other may use the partner benefit if eligible.

Enhanced parental leave > Primary carer benefit

An eligible primary carer may take up to 26 weeks under this enhanced scheme: 12 weeks at full base pay followed by 14 weeks without company pay. Any statutory payment and interaction with this enhancement must be confirmed by the People team. This document does not specify statutory payment rates.

Sickness absence > Evidence

Self-certify absences of up to 7 consecutive calendar days in PeopleHub. For more than 7 consecutive calendar days, provide a fit note covering the absence. Weekends count when determining whether a fit note is required.

Sickness absence > Illness on holiday

For illness during approved annual leave, use the same first-day reporting deadline and evidence rules. The People team reviews reclassification of annual leave; see the annual leave policy. This document does not guarantee that every affected day will be restored.

Annual leave > Illness during leave

If you become ill during approved annual leave, notify your line manager by 10:00 on the first affected working day and follow the sickness reporting policy. The People team reviews requests to reclassify affected days. Reclassification is not automatic.

Business expenses > Home-office purchases

Apply the eligibility, approval and £150 annual limit in the remote working policy before submitting a home-office claim. The £30 meal limit does not apply to home-office equipment. Purchases without the required advance approval are referred to Finance for review; payment is not guaranteed.

Remote and hybrid working > Office attendance

The standard arrangement is at least 2 office days per working week, agreed with your line manager. Employees working fewer than 5 days per week agree an attendance pattern individually; this policy gives no automatic pro-rata formula. Team meetings may require attendance on a specified day.

New starter onboarding > Before day one

The People team sends the contract and right-to-work checklist. Return the requested documents at least 5 working days before your start date. Do not email identity documents to a colleague; use the secure link supplied by the People team.

Annual leave > Contact

Policy owner: Priya Shah, Head of People. Questions: people@northstar-demo.example. This policy contains no live individual leave balances.

Enhanced parental leave > How to request

Notify the People team at least 15 weeks before the expected birth date, or within 7 calendar days of receiving adoption placement notification. Provide the expected date and proposed leave dates. The People team confirms eligibility and the pay schedule in writing.

Remote and hybrid working > Equipment and expenses

IT supplies a managed laptop and one headset. The annual home-office allowance is up to £150 per calendar year for an approved chair, keyboard or monitor. Obtain written line-manager approval before purchase and submit the claim under the expenses policy. Internet subscriptions, electricity and personal phone contracts are not reimbursed.

Remote and hybrid working > Location and availability

Work remotely only from your registered UK home address or another UK location approved in writing by your line manager. Working overseas is not permitted under this policy, including during a holiday. Be available between 10:00 and 15:00 on working days, excluding your agreed lunch break.

Disciplinary procedure > Appeals

The employee may appeal in writing to people@northstar-demo.example within 5 working days of receiving the outcome letter. A manager who was not involved in the investigation or hearing hears the appeal. The appeal decision is final under this procedure.

Disciplinary procedure > Outcomes

Possible outcomes are no action, a first written warning, a final written warning or dismissal. A first written warning stays active for 6 months and a final written warning for 12 months. Gross misconduct may lead to dismissal without prior warnings; examples include harassment or retaliation under the code of conduct and deliberate disclosure of customer data under the information security policy.

Disciplinary procedure > Disciplinary hearing

Give the employee written notice of the hearing at least 3 working days in advance, including the allegations and the evidence. The employee may be accompanied by a work colleague or a trade union representative. A hearing may be rescheduled once, by up to 5 working days, if the companion is unavailable.

Disciplinary procedure > Investigation

Contact the People team before starting any formal action. The People team appoints an investigator within 5 working days. The investigator must not be the employee's line manager or a witness. The employee may be suspended on full base pay only with approval from Priya Shah, Head of People; suspension is not a disciplinary sanction.

Disciplinary procedure > Scope and informal stage

This procedure guides line managers handling suspected misconduct by permanent UK employees. Contractors are managed under their engagement agreement. For minor first concerns, hold an informal conversation and record a summary in PeopleHub within 2 working days. An informal conversation is not a warning.

New starter onboarding > Contacts and scope

For onboarding questions contact people@northstar-demo.example. Use security@northstar-demo.example for suspected security incidents and the 1-hour reporting deadline in the information security policy. This document does not contain live account status, individual salaries or probation outcomes.

Disciplinary procedure > Contact

Procedure owner: Priya Shah, Head of People. Line managers should contact people@northstar-demo.example before any formal step. This document does not contain individual case records.

Annual leave > How to request

Submit requests in PeopleHub at least 10 working days before the first day of leave. Your line manager approves or declines within 3 working days. Do not treat a submitted request as approved. Requests for more than 10 consecutive working days also need approval from Priya Shah, Head of People.

Business expenses > Eligibility and submission

Employees may claim reasonable, necessary business expenses through SpendTrack. Submit claims within 30 calendar days of the purchase date. Attach an itemised receipt and state the business purpose. A missing receipt requires written approval from Finance before submission; a bank statement alone is not an itemised receipt.

Sickness absence > Return to work

Your line manager arranges a return-to-work conversation within 2 working days of your return. Discuss any support or temporary adjustments with the People team. Do not enter private medical details into a public team channel.

New starter onboarding > Before day one

The People team sends the contract and right-to-work checklist. Return the requested documents at least 5 working days before your start date. Do not email identity documents to a colleague; use the secure link supplied by the People team.

Enhanced parental leave > Primary carer benefit

An eligible primary carer may take up to 26 weeks under this enhanced scheme: 12 weeks at full base pay followed by 14 weeks without company pay. Any statutory payment and interaction with this enhancement must be confirmed by the People team. This document does not specify statutory payment rates.

Pay and salary bands > Annual pay review

The annual pay review takes effect on 1 April. Finance confirms the review budget by 31 January. Line managers submit pay proposals in PeopleHub by 28 February; People administrators check them against the bands before approval. Employees who joined after 1 January are not included in that year's review.

Sickness absence > Reporting

If you cannot work because of illness, telephone your line manager by 10:00 on the first affected working day. If they are unavailable, email people@northstar-demo.example by the same deadline. Tell them your likely absence duration if known; you do not need to disclose your diagnosis to colleagues.

Enhanced parental leave > How to request

Notify the People team at least 15 weeks before the expected birth date, or within 7 calendar days of receiving adoption placement notification. Provide the expected date and proposed leave dates. The People team confirms eligibility and the pay schedule in writing.

Enhanced parental leave > Support and return

Contact Priya Shah at people@northstar-demo.example for confidential planning. Discuss your return arrangements at least 4 weeks before returning. Requests for hybrid working are assessed under the remote working policy; parental leave approval does not automatically approve a remote working pattern.

Pay and salary bands > Confidentiality

Band ranges and individual salaries are confidential People team records. Do not share band ranges with employees or line managers outside a formal offer or pay review. An employee may ask the People team for their own salary and band; refer all other salary questions to people@northstar-demo.example.
